title: Japan, Dec 2026 · 8 friends
brief:
# Trip brief

I will be in Tokyo 15–19 Dec, Hakone 19–21, Osaka 21–26 (Osaka base, but during the day we will
commute to Kyoto/Nara as needed, ending the night/nightlife in Osaka; if there are cool nightlife
things to do in the neighbouring cities as well, include them), then Tokyo again 26–29 Dec 2026.

We land at Haneda Terminal 3 on Tue 15 Dec around 15:00 and fly home from Haneda Terminal 3 on
Tue 29 Dec at 17:20.

We are a group of 8, all around 20 years old, all Asian. We love to drink, and we want to maximise
all the time we've got in the country. Think about things like Round1, shopping, and so on; we love
to do it all. No go-karts. Look for money we can save by booking early or buying passes.

Stays (already booked): Ninja House in Toshima (Tokyo), Hot Spring Hakone Villa in Sengokuhara,
Kujō House in Nishi-ku (Osaka), Garfield House in Shinjuku (Tokyo).

stays.name: Ninja House (Airbnb) — Toshima
stays.notes: Ninja House｜2 bathrooms｜near Ikebukuro｜10 guests. Host: Yoko. Keypad self check-in. 9 min walk from Ochiai-minami-nagasaki (Toei Ōedo line) — direct to Shinjuku, Roppongi, Tsukijishijo, Ueno-okachimachi. Free cancellation before Nov 15 4PM.

stays.name: Hot Spring Hakone Villa (Airbnb) — Sengokuhara
stays.notes: Hot Spring Hakone Villa, Easy Access, Piano. Host: Eika. Lockbox self check-in. Access guide was sent in Airbnb messages. Private onsen. Free cancellation before Dec 14 3PM.

stays.name: Kujō House (Airbnb) — Nishi-ku, Osaka
stays.notes: (ちよ)桜と過ごすお部屋 — 4 bedrooms, 2 baths, 4 toilets. Host: Tatsu. Lockbox. Kujō stn (Chūō line + Hanshin Namba line): Namba 6 min, direct trains to Kintetsu-Nara & Kobe-Sannomiya. JR Nishikujō → USJ 10 min. Free cancellation before Nov 21 4PM.

stays.name: Garfield House (Airbnb) — Shinjuku 6-chōme
stays.notes: Garfield home whole build — 10 min walk to Shinjuku-sanchōme. Host: Bibo. Lockbox. Max 8 guests. Walk to Golden Gai / Kabukichō / Ni-chōme. Free cancellation before Nov 26 4PM.

days.title: Romancecar to Hakone · Yumoto soba · Open-Air Museum · Gora craft beer · geisha drinking games · Yumoto highballs

notes.text: Overnight bags only (the suitcases are already on their way to Kujō House). Park them in the Hakone-Yumoto coin lockers after lunch and collect them on the way back down.
The Hakone Freepass covers Odakyu from Shinjuku and every Hakone train today, but Romancecar seats cost extra: reserve all 8 together in advance.

Pre-book two taxis from Yumoto to the villa for the end of the night, and get the villa door code from the host before you leave Tokyo. Dress for a cold mountain evening; it's dark well before dinner.

stops.name: Ninja House
stops.summary: Out the door by 10:00 with overnight bags only, then the Oedo and Marunouchi lines to Shinjuku.
stops.plan: Check out (deadline 10:00) with overnight bags only; the suitcases went to Osaka by TA-Q-BIN on Friday.
stops.transport: Walk to Ochiai-minami-nagasaki, Toei Oedo line → Nakano-sakaue, Tokyo Metro Marunouchi line → Shinjuku, then to the Odakyu Romancecar platforms, about 43 min

guide.story: Last morning in Toshima, travelling light because the big suitcases left for Osaka yesterday. The hop to Shinjuku is two short subway rides, so there's no need to haul anything across the city.
how: Check out before the 10:00 deadline.
Walk to Ochiai-minami-nagasaki and take the Toei Oedo line 10:15→10:21 to Nakano-sakaue.
Change to the Marunouchi line 10:29→10:33 to Shinjuku and follow the signs to the Odakyu Romancecar platforms.
tips: Tap your IC card; the subway leg is ¥290 and isn't covered by the Freepass.
If anyone is running late, a taxi to Shinjuku takes 18 min.
guide.measured: train/bus 43 min door to door (都営大江戸線 落合南長崎→中野坂上 10:15→10:21, 東京メトロ丸ノ内線 中野坂上→新宿 10:29→10:33), ¥290; by taxi 18 min

stops.name: Romancecar Shinjuku → Hakone-Yumoto
stops.summary: Eight seats together on the Romancecar, with ekiben and cold cans, as the city gives way to winter hills.
stops.plan: 8 reserved seats together on the ~11:00 Hakone Romancecar; the 3-day Hakone Freepass on EMot covers the fare. Grab ekiben and cans on the Odakyu concourse.
stops.transport: Walk to Hatsuhana, 8 min

guide.story: The Romancecar is the fun way into Hakone: reserved seats, a picnic on your knees and Tokyo's suburbs thinning out into bare, brown December hills. Since the Freepass already covers the fare, the only add-on is the seat ticket.
how: Pick up the Freepass on EMot and reserve the seat tickets for all 8 together.
Buy ekiben and drinks on the Odakyu concourse before boarding.
Get off at Hakone-Yumoto, the end of the line.
tips: Stock up at Shinjuku; there's little worth buying on board.
Book the seats in advance so the group isn't split across cars on a Saturday.
wishes: Look for money we can save by booking early or buying passes

stops.name: Hatsuhana Soba
stops.summary: Yumoto's classic yam-tororo soba: a warm, cheap first lunch steps from the station.
stops.plan: Yam-tororo soba, Yumoto's classic; take a waitlist ticket, the Shinkan building seats 8.
stops.address: 635-635 Yumoto, 箱根町 Hakone, Ashigarashimo District, Kanagawa 250-0311
stops.transport: Walk back to Hakone-Yumoto Sta. (coin lockers for the bags), Hakone Tozan Railway to Chokoku-no-Mori, about 45 min (Freepass)

guide.story: Hatsuhana is the soba shop Yumoto is known for, a long-running favourite that serves cold-weather bowls of buckwheat noodles under grated mountain yam. It's quick and filling, and the shopping street outside is the place to graze on snacks afterwards.
how: Walk 8 min from Hakone-Yumoto Station.
Take a waitlist ticket at the door; the Shinkan building can seat all 8.
Order the yam-tororo soba.
tips: No bookings, so go straight from the train before the lunch rush builds.
Afterwards, put the bags in the station coin lockers and catch the 14:04 Hakone Tozan train up to Chokoku-no-Mori (arrives 14:39, covered by the Freepass).
guide.booking: No bookings; take a waitlist ticket

facts.text: Regular closing: Thursday (or the day before/after if a holiday); no trip date is a Thursday

guide.measured: train/bus 55 min door to door (箱根登山線 箱根湯本→彫刻の森 14:04→14:39), ¥460; by taxi 18 min

stops.name: Hakone Open-Air Museum
stops.summary: Giant sculptures on a cold hillside, a stained-glass tower to climb, Picasso, and a free footbath to finish.
stops.plan: Sculpture park, the stained-glass Symphonic Sculpture tower and Picasso pavilion; it goes quiet after 15:30, end at the free footbath.
stops.transport: Walk up to Gora Brewery, 16 min

guide.story: Hakone's best museum is mostly outdoors: monumental sculptures scattered across a hillside, with bare winter trees and mountain ridges behind them. The Symphonic Sculpture is a tower wrapped in stained glass that glows when the low December sun hits it, and the Picasso pavilion is a real surprise. The grounds are so big that it rarely feels crowded, and it goes quiet after 15:30.
how: Enter by the main gate and show the Freepass for the discount.
Loop the sculpture park, then climb inside the Symphonic Sculpture tower.
See the Picasso pavilion, then finish with your feet in the free footbath.
tips: An Asoview e-ticket is a little cheaper than paying at the gate.
Do the tower while there's still daylight; the glass is best with the sun on it.
The footbath is the best hand-warmer on the hill, so leave time for it before the 17:00 close.
wishes: We love to do it all

facts.text: Groups: Group admission rate for 15 or more; bus parking needs an advance reservation by FAX

stops.name: Gora Brewery & Grill
stops.summary: Hakone's own brewpub in the Gora woods: house beer flights and wood-fired grill plates as night falls.
stops.plan: Hakone's own brewpub (book a table for 8): a flight of house beers and a few grill plates to share as it gets dark.
stops.transport: Walk to Gora Sta., Hakone Tozan Railway Gora → Hakone-Yumoto (the 18:05), about 55 min door to door (Freepass); collect the bags from the lockers

guide.story: Hidden in the trees uphill from the museum, Gora Brewery opened in 2017 in a building by architect Hiroshi Nakamura with big glass walls onto the forest. The beer is brewed on site, the GORA stout is the one drinkers rave about, and one TikToker called the blistered shishitos the best she's ever had. With the dark coming down outside the glass, it's the best craft-beer stop in Hakone.
how: Walk 16 min uphill from the museum.
Order a flight of the house beers and a spread of grill plates to share; get the shishitos.
Leave in time for the 18:05 Hakone Tozan train from Gora to Yumoto (arrives 18:43, Freepass).
tips: Book the table for 8 ahead; same-day bookings are phone only (0460-83-8107) and there's no guaranteed seat at busy times.
Ask for the stout if you only try one beer.
guide.cost: ¥3,000 pp planned (research puts a full session with beers at ¥4,000–6,000 pp)
guide.booking: Book ahead; same-day by phone only, 0460-83-8107

stops.name: Izakaya Hakoneji
stops.summary: Booked izakaya table in Yumoto: dinner and the first rounds, two minutes from the geisha show.
stops.plan: Booked table for 8: izakaya dinner and the first rounds before the geisha show.
stops.transport: Walk to the Kenban, 2 min

guide.story: Hakoneji is the reliable dinner base for a Yumoto night, an izakaya listed by the official Hakone tourism site that stays open late with no fixed closing day. It's close enough to the Kenban that you can order one more round and still make the show.
how: Grab the bags from the coin lockers when you get off the train, then head to the izakaya.
Order a spread to share and get the first drinks in.
Leave at 19:50 and walk 2 min to the Kenban so all 8 can sit together.
tips: Call ahead to hold a table for 8; it's a Saturday.
Don't linger: doors for the 20:00 show open at 19:30 and the hall is small.
wishes: We love to drink

facts.text: Last entry 23:00
No regular closing day

stops.name: Furatto Geisha night, Hakone Yumoto Kenban
stops.nameJa: 箱根湯本見番「ふらっと芸者」／芸者カフェバーはな
stops.summary: Three geisha dance, then you play their drinking games: Hakone's best night-out, and it's only on tonight.
stops.plan: 3rd-Saturday 20:00 show (doors 19:30, walk over at 19:50 to sit together): three geisha dance, then ozashiki drinking games and photos.
stops.transport: Walk to Flying Chicken, 12 min (or phone for their free pick-up)

guide.story: Yumoto is still a working geisha town, and on the 1st and 3rd Saturday of the month the geisha union opens its Kenban hall to anyone for 'Furatto Geisha'. Tonight is the 3rd Saturday. Three geisha perform a dance, then pull the audience into ozashiki drinking games and pose for photos, with a drink in your hand the whole time.
how: Walk over at 19:50; doors open at 19:30 for the 20:00 show.
Pay at the door: the ticket includes one drink.
Watch the dance, then volunteer for the ozashiki games and stay for photos.
tips: The hall is small, so arriving early is the only way to sit together.
Extra drinks are about ¥700 at the geisha-run Cafe Bar Hana, which is closed on Sundays and Mondays, so tonight is your only chance.
The official page is old; check the time and price before you go.
wishes: If there are cool nightlife things to do in the neighbouring cities as well, include them
We love to drink

stops.name: Flying Chicken (Tori to Highball)
stops.nameJa: 鶏とハイボール フライングチキン
stops.summary: Yakitori and highballs at the one place in Hakone still pouring after the rest of the town has gone to bed.
stops.plan: Yakitori and highballs at Yumoto's one late spot, booked for 8; grab breakfast and cans at a station konbini on the way out.
stops.transport: Taxi to the villa (2 cars, pre-booked; last trains and buses up the mountain are gone), 28 min

guide.story: Yumoto is the only part of Hakone with any late-night life, and Flying Chicken is where it happens: skewers off the grill, highball after highball, open long after the rest of the valley is asleep. The staff will even come and fetch you in their car if you phone from the station.
how: Walk 12 min from the Kenban, or phone 0460-83-8350 for the free pick-up.
Order yakitori in rounds and keep the highballs coming.
Wrap up so the pre-booked taxis can run you to the villa: two cars, 28 min.
tips: Book for 8 by phone and ask about the pick-up at the same time.
The last trains and buses up the mountain are gone by then; a taxi to Sengokuhara is about ¥7,000–9,000 per car.
Grab tomorrow's breakfast and cans at a station konbini on the way out.
guide.hours: From the evening; listings give 02:00 or 03:00 closing
wishes: We love to drink

stops.name: Hot Spring Hakone Villa
stops.summary: Late self check-in, then a midnight soak in the villa's own hot spring.
stops.plan: Late self check-in (confirm the door code with the host), then a midnight soak in the villa's own hot spring.

guide.story: After a cold day and a long night, the villa's private hot spring is the reward: steam rising into the dark Sengokuhara air, and nobody else's schedule but yours.
how: Let yourselves in with the door code from the host.
Drop the bags and head straight for the bath.
tips: Confirm the door code before you leave Yumoto; there's no phone signal you want to rely on at midnight.
wishes: Stays already booked: Ninja House in Toshima (Tokyo), Hot Spring Hakone Villa in Sengokuhara, Kujō House in Nishi-ku (Osaka), Garfield House in Shinjuku (Tokyo)

days.title: First ropeway to Owakudani · pirate ship across Lake Ashi · lakeside torii · castle-villa lunch · Glass no Mori lights · Sengokuhara sushi · snack-bar karaoke

notes.text: Owakudani is cold, windy and sulphurous at 9am: hats, gloves, the warmest layer you packed. It's dark by 16:45.
Confirm the Albergo Bamboo private room, and call Snack Takachan (0460-83-8677) by tonight at the latest about a set price for 8 and a lift.
The Freepass covers the bus, ropeway and pirate ship. The two taxis from Hakone Shrine to Sengokuhara are extra, and so is everything you eat and drink.

stops.name: Hot Spring Hakone Villa
stops.plan: Konbini breakfast from last night's haul and a quick morning soak; dress warm, Owakudani is cold and windy.
stops.transport: Hakone Tozan bus to Togendai (Freepass), or a 30-min walk downhill

stops.name: Hakone Ropeway Togendai → Owakudani
stops.summary: First ropeway car up, sitting on the lake side, for the clearest Fuji views you'll get all trip.
stops.plan: First car up (December service 9:00–16:15, Freepass); sit facing the lake for Fuji. The Owakudani–Sōunzan leg beyond is a replacement bus 7–24 Dec, so we only ride up and back.
stops.transport: Arrive at Owakudani station

guide.story: December mornings are when Fuji is at its sharpest. From the first gondola you watch Lake Ashi drop away behind you while the white cone rises over the ridge. The Owakudani–Sōunzan leg beyond is a replacement bus 7–24 Dec, so today you ride up and come back the same way.
how: Get to Togendai for the first car at 9:00 and show your Freepass at the gate.
Grab the seats facing the lake so you're looking towards Fuji.
Get off at Owakudani. Don't try to carry on towards Sōunzan.
tips: Gondolas run continuously, so all 8 of you can split across two cars and meet at the top.
December service runs 9:00–16:15. If it's suspended for wind, go straight to the pirate ship.
wishes: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country
We love to do it all

stops.name: Owakudani & black eggs
stops.nameJa: 箱根ロープウェイ・大涌谷
stops.summary: Steaming sulphur vents, Fuji over the ridge, and kuro-tamago eggs boiled black in the volcanic pools.
stops.plan: Sulphur vents and the clearest Fuji views of the day; kuro-tamago black eggs and souvenir shopping at the station shop.
stops.transport: Hakone Ropeway Owakudani → Togendai, about 25 min (Freepass)

guide.story: Owakudani is a raw volcanic crater: yellow rock, hissing vents, and steam blowing sideways in the winter wind. The kuro-tamago come out of the hot spring water with jet-black shells and ordinary white egg inside. Eating one with Fuji in view is the Hakone ritual.
how: Follow the path to the viewing area for the vents with Fuji behind.
Buy black eggs at the station shop: ¥500 for a bag of 5, so two bags covers 8 with spares.
Do your souvenir shopping before you ride back down to Togendai.
tips: Your hands will be freezing, so peel the eggs indoors.
The sulphur smell gets into scarves. Don't wear your nicest one.
The ropeway can stop in bad weather, so keep an eye on the boards.
wishes: We love to do it all
Shopping

stops.name: Pirate ship Togendai → Motohakone
stops.summary: A mock galleon across a steel-grey winter Lake Ashi, with Fuji off the stern if the sky holds.
stops.plan: Next winter-schedule sailing from Togendai (Freepass; winter crossings run slower); deck up top for the lake and Fuji.
stops.address: 箱根町元箱根164桃源台港
stops.transport: Walk along the lakeshore to Hakone Shrine, 6 min

guide.story: It's kitsch and everyone knows it: a gilded pirate ship chugging across a cold mountain lake. That's the fun. On a clear December morning the top deck gets the lake, the bare hills and Fuji all in one frame.
how: Board at Togendai for the next winter sailing. The Freepass covers it.
Go straight up to the open top deck.
Get off at Motohakone. Hakone Shrine is a 6-min walk along the shore.
tips: The first-class deck upgrade costs extra and isn't worth it for a crossing this short.
It's windy out on the water. Go back inside once you've got your photos.
wishes: We love to do it all

facts.text: Sailings can be suspended in bad weather

stops.name: Hakone Shrine & Torii of Peace
stops.nameJa: 箱根神社 平和の鳥居
stops.summary: Cedar-lined steps to Hakone Shrine and the red torii standing in the lake, without the midday queue.
stops.plan: Cedar-lined steps to the shrine, then shoot the lakeside torii from the side path instead of the midday photo queue.
stops.transport: Taxi to Sengokuhara (2 cars), 23 min

guide.story: Huge old cedars shade the stone steps up to the shrine, which feels quiet and ancient even when the shore is busy. Below it, the red Torii of Peace stands right in Lake Ashi, Hakone's signature photo. By midday the line to pose under it can run 30–90 minutes.
how: Walk up the cedar approach to the main shrine. It's free.
For the torii, skip the queue and shoot it from the side path.
Order the two taxis to Sengokuhara from the shore. It's a 23-min ride.
tips: If you really want the posed shot, send one person to hold your place in the queue while the others explore.
The treasure hall is ¥500 if anyone wants to go in.
wishes: We love to do it all

stops.name: Albergo Bamboo
stops.nameJa: アルベルゴ・バンブー
stops.summary: The splurge lunch: a castle-style Italian villa with uni-lemon cream pasta and winter boar in a private room.
stops.plan: Booked upstairs private room for 8 in the castle-style villa: uni-lemon cream pasta, winter boar, a bottle of prosecco.
stops.transport: Walk to Hakone Glass no Mori, 9 min

guide.story: Albergo Bamboo looks like a small European castle dropped into the Hakone woods, and TV dramas film here. Upstairs you have the private room to yourselves. The uni and lemon cream pasta is the dish people come for, and in winter the menu adds boar and venison.
how: Arrive for your booked upstairs private room for 8.
Order the uni-lemon cream pasta, the winter boar, and a bottle of prosecco for the table.
Lunch last orders are 14:30, so don't be late. Glass no Mori is a 9-min walk.
tips: Dress up a bit: this is the group photo meal of the Hakone stay.
Booking is by phone (0460-84-3311) or the online form on the official site.

wishes: We love to drink

stops.name: Hakone Glass no Mori Christmas illumination
stops.nameJa: 箱根ガラスの森美術館 クリスタルイルミネーション
stops.summary: A Venetian-glass garden of crystal arches and a glass Christmas tree that lights up around sunset.
stops.plan: Venetian glass garden and crystal arches; stay past sunset (~16:30) for the glass Christmas tree and candles (lit 1–25 Dec).
stops.transport: Walk to A-Coop, 15 min

guide.story: Crystal-strung arches and a big glass Christmas tree glitter under the low winter sun, then sparkle again once the lights come on. Candles are lit only 1–25 Dec, so you're catching it at its best. With sunset around 16:30 you see it in daylight and after dark.
how: Show your Freepass at the ticket desk for the ¥100 discount: ¥1,700 pp (the full adult price is ¥1,800).
Walk the garden in daylight first, then wait by the glass tree as it gets dark around 16:30.
Leave at 16:35 so you reach A-Coop with time to spare.
tips: Golden hour just before dusk is the photo slot.
Last entry is 17:00, but you'll be gone by then. Don't let anyone wander off.
wishes: We love to do it all
We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

stops.name: A-Coop Sengokuhara
stops.summary: The village's only supermarket: tomorrow's breakfast and the villa's drinks, before the 18:00 close.
stops.plan: Before the 18:00 close: tomorrow's breakfast plus cans, chu-hi and sake for the villa (Yamakawaya is shut on Sundays).
stops.transport: Walk to Hakone Sushi, 12 min

guide.story: A-Coop is Sengokuhara's only supermarket, and it closes early. It's Sunday, so Yamakawaya is shut too. Miss this and tonight's nightcaps are gone.
how: Split up: two people on breakfast, the rest on cans, chu-hi and sake.
Get breakfast for tomorrow morning, because check-out is 10:00.
Hakone Sushi is a 12-min walk from here.
tips: Stock runs out late in the day, so grab the drinks first.
It's open 9:30–18:00, so don't let Glass no Mori run late.

stops.name: Hakone Sushi
stops.summary: Father-and-son sushi that locals call the place in Sengokuhara: special chirashi, uni-ikura and anago.
stops.plan: Booked tatami room for 8 (phone 0460-84-7890): special chirashi, uni-ikura bowls, anago and local sake.
stops.transport: Walk to Snack Takachan, 14 min

guide.story: Hakone Sushi has been run by a father and son for 30 years, and it's full most nights even midweek. The special-grade chirashi is ¥3,500, the uni-ikura bowl is the showpiece, and the anago is what regulars order again. With local sake in a tatami room, it feels like a real mountain-village dinner.
how: Go to your booked tatami room for 8.
Order the special chirashi and the uni-ikura bowls, plus anago for the table.
Ask for local sake. Last order is 20:00.
Snack Takachan is a 14-min walk.
tips: They don't take bookings by DM. Call 0460-84-7890.
Credit cards are accepted.

stops.name: Snack Takachan & Maron
stops.nameJa: スナック たかちゃん&まろん
stops.summary: A mama-san snack bar with karaoke, the only real night out in Sengokuhara. Eight of you basically take it over.
stops.plan: Book the night before: mama-san snack bar with karaoke, ask for a set price for 8 and a lift back to the villa.
stops.transport: Taxi or the bar's lift to the villa, 6 min

guide.story: A Japanese snack bar is a tiny room with a mama-san behind the counter and a karaoke machine. With 8 of you it turns into a private karaoke party in a mountain village where nothing else is open. It's open until 2:00, and the bar can drive you home by arrangement.
how: Call 0460-83-8677 the day before and ask for a set price or nomihodai for 8.
Ask about a pick-up (送迎) back to the villa when you call.
Sing something the mama-san knows. It goes down well.
tips: Settle the set price before the first round so the bill is no surprise.
It's a small bar, so be loud in the karaoke and polite between songs.
wishes: We love to drink
We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

stops.name: Hot Spring Hakone Villa
stops.plan: Last soak and nightcaps; pack tonight, check-out is 10:00 tomorrow.

days.title: Gotemba outlet haul · Hikari to Osaka · Tenma fish feast, standing-bar crawl and OWL

notes.text: Tax-free at Gotemba: each person pays full price with their own passport; keep the goods unused with receipts in your carry-on for the Haneda customs kiosk, never in the TA-Q-BIN suitcases.
Cold, clear December day: Fuji is sharpest over the outlets in the morning, and it's dark before the Shinkansen even leaves Mishima. Wear layers you can shove in a bag.
Original passports all day: tax-free at the outlets, then the OWL door tonight.

stops.name: Breakfast and last soak at the villa
stops.plan: Breakfast from the groceries bought on the way up, one last hot-spring soak, then pack the overnight bags.

stops.name: Check out Hot Spring Hakone Villa
stops.summary: Out of the villa with overnight bags only and onto the Tozan bus down to Gotemba.
stops.plan: Out by 10:00 with the overnight bags; the suitcases are already on their way to Kujō by TA-Q-BIN.
stops.transport: Hakone Tozan bus Sengokuhara → Gotemba Premium Outlets, about 35–50 min with the wait (Hakone Freepass day 3; if it doesn't cover this stretch, pay by IC card)

guide.story: The big suitcases are already riding Yamato's trucks to Kujō House, so this is a light-footed exit: overnight bags and that last hot-spring glow. Sengokuhara in December is pampas grass gone silver-brown and frost on the shade side of the road.
how: Out by 10:00; do a last sweep of the bathroom and fridge.
Take the Hakone Tozan bus from Sengokuhara to Gotemba Premium Outlets; try the Hakone Freepass first, and tap IC cards if the driver says it isn't covered.
tips: Sit on the left side heading down for the best shot of Fuji over the Gotemba plain if the sky is clear.
wishes: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

stops.name: Gotemba Premium Outlets
stops.summary: Japan's Fuji-backed outlet mall: two squads of four, app coupons first, then Nike, New Balance and Beams.
stops.plan: Coin-locker the overnight bags, then split into two squads of four for Nike, New Balance, Beams and the rest; get the app coupons first and carry passports for tax-free.

guide.story: Gotemba Premium Outlets is a sprawling open-air village with Mount Fuji filling the sky behind the shopfronts, and on a cold clear December morning the snowcap looks close enough to touch. This is the trip's big haul window before Osaka, so move with purpose.
how: Find coin lockers by the entrance and stash the overnight bags before anything else.
Download the outlet app and grab the coupons before your first till.
Split into two squads of four: one runs sportswear (Nike, New Balance), the other fashion (Beams and the rest); share a group chat for finds and sizes.
tips: Tax-free can't be pooled: whoever wears it pays for it with their own passport.
Hit the sportswear stores first; sizes thin out fast once the tour buses arrive.
Keep receipts with the goods; they all go home in carry-ons.
wishes: Shopping
We love to do it all

stops.name: Lunch at the outlets' food court
stops.summary: Quick food-court regroup: refuel, compare hauls, plan the second sweep.
stops.plan: Regroup for a quick food-court lunch and compare hauls.

guide.story: The food court is the one warm, sit-down spot in the whole place, and the half-hour where everyone dumps their bags and shows off what they found. Keep it quick; the second round is where the real deals turn up.
how: Grab tables first, then send people to order in turns.
Swap tips on which shops still have stock and sizes.
tips: Budget ¥1,500 pp.
wishes: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

stops.name: Gotemba Premium Outlets, round two
stops.summary: Second sweep for what you missed; taxi stand with every bag at 14:50 sharp.
stops.plan: Second sweep for the shops you missed; meet at the taxi stand with bags at 14:50 sharp.
stops.transport: Taxi to Mishima Station, 29 min (2 cars; the trains take over 2 hours via the JR Gotemba line)

guide.story: Round two is for the stores you walked past and the size you talked yourself out of at lunch. Afternoon light goes low and gold over Fuji in December, so grab the group photo before you go.
how: Hit the shops your squad skipped this morning.
Collect bags from the lockers before heading to the taxi stand.
Two taxis to Mishima Station, 29 min; the train alternative takes 128 min door to door, so don't.
tips: Be at the taxi stand at 14:50 sharp; the Shinkansen seats are reserved and won't wait.
wishes: Shopping
guide.measured: train/bus 128 min door to door (ＪＲ御殿場線 御殿場→下土狩 16:10→16:38), ¥420; by taxi 29 min

stops.name: Hikari 717 Mishima → Shin-Osaka
stops.summary: Hikari 717 to Shin-Osaka: eight reserved seats together, drinks from Mishima, Osaka by 17:57.
stops.plan: Reserved seats for all 8 together, booked ahead; buy drinks and snacks at Mishima for the ride.
stops.transport: Osaka Metro Midosuji line Shin-Osaka → Hommachi, Chuo line → Kujō, about 38 min door to door · timetable: OsakaMetro御堂筋線 新大阪→本町 18:17→18:27, OsakaMetro中央線 本町→九条（大阪府） 18:34→18:39 · ¥290

guide.story: Two-plus hours of Shinkansen with the shopping bags at your feet and Fuji falling away behind you in the last of the light; by the time you pass Nagoya it's full dark outside. This is the trip's prime pre-game window.
how: Buy beers, highballs and snacks at Mishima station before boarding.
Find your reserved car and sit together; the outlet bags go in the overhead racks.
At Shin-Osaka take the Midosuji line to Hommachi, then the Chuo line to Kujō.
tips: Snap Fuji from the right-hand side of the train as you pull out of Mishima, before the light goes.
Correction: Cold, clear December day: Fuji is sharpest over the outlets in the morning, and the sun sets around 16:37, shortly after the Hikari leaves Mishima at 15:46, so it is dark by Nagoya.
guide.booking: Reserved seats for all 8 together, booked ahead
wishes: We love to drink
We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country

facts.text: Cold, clear December day: Fuji is sharpest over the outlets in the morning, and the sun sets around 16:37, shortly after the Hikari leaves Mishima at 15:46, so it is dark by Nagoya.

guide.measured: train/bus 38 min door to door (OsakaMetro御堂筋線 新大阪→本町 18:17→18:27, OsakaMetro中央線 本町→九条（大阪府） 18:34→18:39), ¥290; by taxi 19 min

stops.name: Check in Kujō House
stops.summary: Check in, reunite with the suitcases, change, and grab original passports for tonight.
stops.plan: Check in, collect the TA-Q-BIN suitcases, drop the outlet bags, change for the night and grab original passports.
stops.transport: Osaka Metro Chuo line Kujō → Sakaisuji-Hommachi, Sakaisuji line → Tenjinbashisuji 6-chome, about 32 min · timetable: OsakaMetro中央線 九条（大阪府）→堺筋本町 19:40→19:46, OsakaMetro堺筋線 堺筋本町→天神橋筋六丁目 19:50→19:56 · ¥240

guide.story: The TA-Q-BIN suitcases should be waiting, which means a quick change into night-out gear before heading north to Tenma.
how: Collect the suitcases and drop the outlet bags; tax-free goods stay unopened.
Change, then take original passports: OWL checks them at the door.
Chuo line to Sakaisuji-Hommachi, then the Sakaisuji line to Tenjinbashisuji 6-chome.
tips: Taxi to Tenma is 14 min if anyone runs late.
wishes: Stays already booked: Ninja House in Toshima (Tokyo), Hot Spring Hakone Villa in Sengokuhara, Kujō House in Nishi-ku (Osaka), Garfield House in Shinjuku (Tokyo)
guide.measured: train/bus 37 min door to door (OsakaMetro中央線 九条（大阪府）→堺筋本町 19:40→19:46, OsakaMetro堺筋線 堺筋本町→天神橋筋六丁目 19:50→19:56), ¥240; by taxi 14 min

stops.name: Sakanaya Juggler Tenma
stops.nameJa: 魚屋 ジャグラー 天満
stops.summary: First Osaka dinner: a cheap fish izakaya open till 3am with a booked table for 8.
stops.plan: Booked table for 8: cheap sashimi, grilled fish and highballs for the first Osaka dinner together.
stops.transport: Walk to the Ura-Tenma alleys, 4 min

guide.story: Sakanaya Juggler is the kind of Tenma fish joint where the prices are so low you read the menu five times, with sashimi, grilled fish and highballs flowing at about ¥3,000 a head. It takes reservations, which is rare for a place this cheap and this good for a group of eight.
how: Booked table for 8 under your name; arrive on time.
Start with a sashimi platter and highballs, then grilled fish.
Leave on schedule: the standing-bar alleys are a 4 min walk.
tips: Rated 4.5 on Google Places.
Open till 03:00, so it doubles as a late-night fallback after the crawl.
guide.booking: Reservations accepted (06-6948-8662); ask for a table for 8
wishes: We love to drink

stops.name: Ura-Tenma standing-bar alleys
stops.nameJa: 裏天満（天満 立ち飲み街）
stops.summary: Osaka's best-value drinking maze: tarp-roofed standing bars, big bottles of beer and horumon skewers.
stops.plan: Split 2×4 and hop the tachinomi around Tenma Market: big bottles of beer and horumon skewers, swap bars every half hour, cash only.
stops.transport: JR Osaka Loop line Tenma → Osaka and walk, about 25 min

guide.story: North of JR Tenma, around Tenma Market, the alleys are packed with tachinomi under tarp sheets and the glow of horumon grills, where locals stand shoulder to shoulder and talk to whoever's next to them. On a cold December night the heaters and smoke make it feel like a single giant bar.
how: Split into 2×4: standing bars rarely have a gap for eight.
Swap bars every half hour; look for Daian, Dengeki Horumon Tsugie and Tokuichi.
Order big bottles of beer to share, from ¥330 at the old-school bars.
tips: Cash only.
Many bars close by 23:00, so start the crawl straight after dinner.
Dengeki Horumon Tsugie draws a young crowd, with skewers at ¥300–900.
wishes: We love to drink
We love to do it all
guide.measured: train/bus 25 min door to door (ＪＲ大阪環状線 天満→大阪 23:18→23:21), ¥150; by taxi 8 min

stops.name: OWL Osaka (Umeda club)
stops.summary: First Osaka club night: OWL in Umeda, mainstream EDM and hip-hop, open every night.
stops.plan: First Osaka club night (open nightly); original passports for the door and bag check; leave at 01:30 because USJ is tomorrow morning.
stops.address: 〒530-0017 Osaka, Kita Ward, Kakudachō, 5−１ Umedarakutenchi Building, B1
stops.transport: Taxi to Kujō House, 14 min (2 cars, about ¥2,300 each)

guide.story: OWL is the big Kita club, mainstream EDM and hip-hop with a crowd full of first-timers, which makes it an easy landing for a Monday when the Minami clubs are quiet. Rated 4.3 on Google Places from 807 reviews.
how: JR Loop line Tenma → Osaka (23:18→23:21, ¥150), then walk.
Original passports ready; everyone's bags get checked at the door.
Leave at 01:30: USJ is tomorrow morning.
tips: Advance foreigner tickets via Expedia, Headout or TryHard beat the door price.
VIP reservations open 1 week ahead (tel 06-6362-0822).
Two taxis back to Kujō House.

coverage.wish: Osaka base, but during the day we will commute to Kyoto/Nara as needed
coverage.how: Osaka base at Kujō House with day trips: USJ (22 Dec), Kyoto from Fushimi Inari to Kiyamachi (23 Dec), Nara Park and Todai-ji (24 Dec).

Every Osaka night ends in Osaka: Tenma and OWL (21), Dotonbori and Jankara (22), Giraffe and Kinryu ramen (24), Ura-Namba, Circus and Round1 to the first train (25). The Kyoto night returns on the 23:00 Keihan.

coverage.wish: If there are cool nightlife things to do in the neighbouring cities as well, include them
coverage.how: Kyoto nightlife on 23 Dec: Pontocho at dusk, Kiyamachi izakaya and bars, then Kitsune Kyoto before the last train. Hakone nights: Gora Brewery, the geisha night and Flying Chicken (19), snack-bar karaoke (20).

Drinking every night: all-you-can-drink courses (Kingyuen, Mugen Gyoza, Kiyamachi, Umi no Ie), yokocho crawls (Shibuya, Ebisu, Ameyoko, Ura-Tenma, Ura-Namba, Omoide, Golden Gai), five club nights (ZEROTOKYO twice, OWL, Giraffe, Circus, ATOM).

coverage.wish: We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country
coverage.how: Packed days from early starts to late nights on all 15 dates, routed one area at a time with measured travel so no time is lost doubling back; the arrival evening and departure morning are used too.
Round1 Ikebukuro on the first night (15 Dec) and Round1 Sennichimae until the first train on Christmas night (25 Dec).

Boro-ichi and Shimokitazawa (16), Akihabara and Ameyoko (18), Gotemba Premium Outlets (21), Kyoto arcades and Nintendo KYOTO (23), Den Den Town, Shinsaibashi and Ame-mura (24), Koenji, Nakano Broadway, Harajuku, MEGA Donki (28), Isetan and Donki (29).

coverage.wish: We love to do it all
coverage.how: A bit of everything: theme park, onsen (Manyo Club, the villa), geisha games, ropeway and pirate ship, shrines and temples, Christmas markets and illuminations, fireworks, food crawls, clubs and karaoke.
No go-karts anywhere in the plan.

coverage.wish: Look for money we can save by booking early or buying passes
coverage.how: Savings: Hakone Freepass (transport plus museum discounts), Enoshima-Kamakura Freepass, Round1 and Jankara app prices, online-only cheaper Shibuya Sky ticket, advance club tickets, all-you-can-drink courses, tax-free refunds at Haneda. Booking dates are in the to-dos.
